_note: Generic Mesopotamian base culture (BASE_03), single-language Akkadian from culture_hammuran.json (kept separately). The seed-stock from which the Near-Eastern (Akkadian) hybrids emerge: river-valley city-states and law-giving empires - the alu-cities and the bit-ili temples, the sharru on the throne and the hazannu over the town. civ = feudal. Even split across all three alignments. Common-word lexicon and rank titles use the real Akkadian register (allowed, catalog 5.3); DEITY names are phoneme-morphs of the canonical (Agrippan) pantheon through Akkadian phonology (gdd-naming-conventions 5), never real Mesopotamian gods. Ruler/domain DISPLAY titles are English; the Akkadian forms are in ruler_native/domain_native for NPC dialogue only.

phonology.palette: Akkadian: sh, ', kh, ts, q; vowels a i u; endings -u/-tu/-um; theophoric stems are morphed canon-names (Tullaru-, Argantu-, Urlandu-, Numunu-).
phonology.phonotactics: CVC; mimation -um; construct chains; stress penultimate.

morphology.patronymic_form: patronymic 'mar' (son of); theophoric given names (on morphed god-stems); family/profession house.
morphology.compounding_rule: construct chains: Bit-[god/name] (house of), Dur-[ruler] (fort of), Kar-[god] (port of); resource + feature.

title_ladder.government: feudal (Mesopotamian; the law-code and temple-bureaucracy character is narrative flavor - the sharru at the crown, the hazannu over the alu-town, the sangu-priesthood serving in the bit-ili)
title_ladder._tiers_note: Akkadian native ladder, ascending (barony, march, county, duchy, principality, kingdom, empire). -u/-utu rhyme (Hazannu/Hazannutu ... Sharru/Sharrutu). Hazannu (mayor) barony; Massaru (warden) march; Shaknu (appointed governor) county; Turtanu (commander-in-chief) duchy; Rubu (prince) principality; Sharru (king) kingdom; Shar-kishshati (king of the totality) emperor over the Kishshatu. (Rank titles are the real Akkadian register, allowed.) DISPLAY titles are English per display_policy; the Akkadian forms above are for NPC dialogue only.
title_ladder.heir: Mar-Sharri (son of the king / crown prince)
title_ladder.display_policy: Ruler/domain titles shown in setting-gen, domain lists and vassal trees are ENGLISH. The *_native conlang forms are for NPC DIALOGUE ONLY, never for structural/UI displays.

people_name_convention.dual_register: officials use a profession/house title; commoners a patronymic.
people_name_convention.theophoric: given names built from the morphed deity-names + a common Akkadian verb: X-iddina (X-gave), X-uballit (X-kept-alive), Warad-X (servant-of-X). e.g. Tullaru-iddina, Warad-Urlandu.

religion._note: Deity-names are phoneme-morphs of the canonical (Agrippan) pantheon through Akkadian phonology (-us/-ius -> -u/-ishu; o -> u; v -> b; doubling) - recognizably the same powers, never real Mesopotamian gods. All three alignments.
religion.the_one: Itarnu (< Aeternus; the great distant one, honored not petitioned)

worship_by_alignment.Lawful: venerates the Lawful powers of the canon - Itarnu the distant, Tullaru the just sun-judge, Urlandu of the sworn war, Rialtu the merciful - and names the Chaotic powers -lemnu (evil), warded by the law-stele and the temple rite
worship_by_alignment.Neutral: the city-spirits and ancestral dead of the bit-ili and the family stele; the great powers invoked at the temple situationally, as the season and the need require
worship_by_alignment.Chaotic: Venerates the Chaotic powers of the canon, and names the Lawful powers - and Itarnu - as the tyrant-gods to be defied.

religion.demon_epithet_pattern: each opposing power keeps its morphed name + its own portfolio epithet (distinct per power; the suffix '-lemnu' = evil may be appended): Maraxus -> Marakshu the City-Burner; Irantius -> Irantishu the Restless; Vacidus -> Bakidu-lemnu (the Unmaking).
religion.religious_orders_pattern: the Bit-ili (god-house/temple) of [power]: 'the Bit-ili of Tullaru'.
religion.saints_pattern: deified law-givers and heroes inscribed on the temple-stele; 'the Just [name]'.

banks_patterns.ships: river-barge names: 'Pride of the Naru', 'Boat of Tullaru'
banks_patterns.military_units: the [god] Standard / the [number] Companies: 'the Standard of Urlandu'
banks_patterns.dungeons_ruins: buried ziggurats and dead cities: 'the Ziggurat of Dur-[name]', 'the Sunken Ekallu'
